title: The Art of Prompt Engineering
subtitle: Tokens, the context window, your first API key — then a build day: structured output, a focus group from your own idea, a photo that becomes data, and your first agent
heroTitle: The Art of Prompt Engineering

objectives.title: See What the Chatbot Hides
objectives.description: Tokens, the context window, and in-context learning — why AI is billed the way it is, why it forgets, and why three examples in a prompt can reprogram a model with zero training.

objectives.title: Get Your First API Key
objectives.description: A free Google AI Studio key, stored the professional way in Colab Secrets. Then your own Python talks to a frontier model — the foundation for agents, RAG, and your final project.

objectives.title: Make the Model Fill In a Form
objectives.description: Structured output: hand Gemini a schema and get guaranteed JSON back — a support ticket from a messy email, 25 customer reactions from one call, a receipt from a phone photo. The bridge from AI to your systems.

objectives.title: Build Your First Agent
objectives.description: Give the model tools and watch it decide — which to call, when, and whether it is done. You read the ~40-line loop that is inside every agent on Earth.

agenda.title: Meeting 1 · HW #3 Debrief + Three Secrets
agenda.description: Your model-picker memos, then the three things your chatbot never told you: tokens, the context window, and in-context learning.
bulletPoints: Live tokenizer: why 'strawberry' breaks letter-counting and why some languages cost 3x more
Context window: your TinyGPT remembered 16 letters; Fable remembers a million tokens — same rule
In-context learning: three examples in the prompt reprogram the model with zero training

agenda.title: The Rite of Passage: Your First API Key
agenda.description: Everyone gets a free Google AI Studio key into Colab Secrets, then your own code talks to a frontier model.
bulletPoints: aistudio.google.com → key → Colab 🔑 Secrets (never in code)
First call, the temperature dial you already know, and the token meter — price a call like a CFO
One system instruction = a different product

agenda.title: Wrap: Six Lines Is the Moat + HW #4
agenda.description: The distance from AI user to AI builder, in business terms — and the Tokenizer Safari.
bulletPoints: HW #4: tokenizer safari — one surprising screenshot + a pricing implication, due Thu Oct 1, 11:59 PM

agenda.title: Meeting 2 · Build Day, Part A: You Are the Loop
agenda.description: Everyone confirms a working key, then: pitch YOUR idea to 25 synthetic customers, chart the objections, fix the pitch, re-run the same room.
bulletPoints: Prose is for people, data is for systems — the model fills in a schema you designed
Would they pay, at what price, their #1 objection in their own voice — one call, 25 rows, a chart
The honesty check: a hypothesis, not evidence — and exactly what to ask five real people

agenda.title: Part B: The Model Is the Loop
agenda.description: Hand the model the focus group as a tool and one goal. Press play. It decides when to run the room, what to change, and when to stop — your first agent. Then an audit checks whether it cheated.
bulletPoints: LLM + Tools + Loop + Memory = Agent — nobody wrote an if-statement
Every 'the model chose:' line in the trace is a decision you didn't code
Goodhart's law, live: give an agent a number and it finds the cheapest way to move it — why humans approve

agenda.title: Wrap: Boardroom + Wednesday
agenda.description: If ahead, a phone photo of a receipt becomes a table. Then what you can now say in a meeting, and Wednesday: you write the 40-line loop yourself, then make it enterprise-grade.
bulletPoints: "Can we just let the agent optimize it?" — only with an audit and a human gate
HW #4 (Tokenizer Safari) due Thu Oct 1, 11:59 PM — last call

activities.title: Tokenizer Safari (live, then HW #4)
activities.description: Watch text become tokens and connect it to the bill:

steps.title: Paste an English sentence
steps.description: Count the tokens. Roughly three-quarters of a word each.

steps.title: Same idea in another language you know
steps.description: More tokens for the same meaning — some languages cost 2–3× more per sentence.

steps.title: Something weird
steps.description: Code, emoji, names. Then strawberry: the model sees [straw][berry], not letters.

steps.title: Tie it back
steps.description: Your TinyGPT's tokens were single letters (vocabulary 27). Frontier models use ~100,000 chunks. Same idea.

steps.description: Your code sends a request across the internet, a datacenter runs inference, the answer comes back. You just crossed the line.

takeaways.text: Tokens are the unit of everything. Cost, rate limits, and memory are all measured in tokens — and some languages cost 2–3× more.
The context window is the whole memory. What falls out is gone. The fix at scale is retrieval, not bigger prompts.
Examples are programming. A few examples in the prompt change behavior with zero training — cheaper, faster, and reversible compared with fine-tuning.
Prose is for people, data is for systems. Hand the model a schema and it fills in the form — that is the bridge from AI to your dashboards, databases, and spreadsheets.
Six lines is the moat. The distance from AI user to AI builder is one API key and one call. You crossed it.

Nobody wrote an if-statement. Give the model a tool and a goal, and it decides which to call, when, and whether it is done. That is an agent — and it will game any metric you hand it, which is why humans approve.
